children: Shares of Maharaja & Speedex India hit the 5 per cent upper circuit limit on Friday after making a 34 per cent gain on their listing debut.
The stock quoted at Rs 262.50 per share on the BSE SME platform, up 5 per cent from its previous close and at its highest permissible trading limit for the session.
Shares of the company had listed at Rs 250 per share, a premium of 34 per cent over the issue price.

The Maharaja & Speedex India IPO was valued at Rs 80.13 crore. The issue comprised a fresh issue of 34.46 lakh shares worth Rs 64.10 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 8.62 lakh shares valued at Rs 16.03 crore.

The IPO was offered in a price band of Rs 177-186 per share, with a lot size of 600 shares. At the upper end of the price band, the minimum retail investment was Rs 2,23,200 for an application of 1,200 shares.

The issue was subscribed 32.41 times overall. It received 19.65 times subscription from individual investors, 48.82 times from qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), excluding the anchor portion, and 40.32 times from non-institutional investors (NIIs).
In the grey market, the Maharaja & Speedex India IPO was commanding a premium of 15 per cent.

title: Maharaja & Speedex SME shares hit upper circuit post 34% listing gains on debut day
